growth.basis: least-squares fit over the readings stored for this spot

rain.note: Monthly normal for New Delhi, 0 km away, apportioned across the 14 days. A normal is what a fortnight like this usually brings, not a forecast. Post a real forecast to /api/rainfall and it is used instead.

traffic.note: No road class and no count. Treated as a residential lane at 300 commercial vehicles a day, which is the reference road — the traffic term is 1.0 and changes nothing.

summary.formula: priority = growth rate (mm/day) × rainfall factor × traffic factor

terms.growth: Millimetres a day, from a least-squares fit over the readings actually stored for that spot. Measured, not modelled.
terms.rain: 1 + expected millimetres over the next 14 days / 60, capped at 5. One in a dry fortnight, so a dry-season priority is growth × traffic and nothing invented.
terms.traffic: sqrt(commercial vehicles per day / 300), clamped 0.5 to 4.0. A residential lane is exactly 1.
terms.score: The product is an effective growth rate in mm/day, mapped to 0-100 on a log scale: 0.05 mm/day scores 0, 10 mm/day scores 100. Logarithmic because the product spans orders of magnitude and a straight line would pin every spot worth looking at to 100.

road_classes.label: National highway
road_classes.about: Through freight. Heaviest axle loads on the network.

road_classes.label: Major district road
road_classes.about: Feeds the highway network; loaded local freight.

road_classes.label: Urban arterial
road_classes.about: City spine — buses, tippers, delivery trucks all day.

road_classes.label: Residential lane
road_classes.about: The reference road. Waste truck, autos, two-wheelers.

road_classes.label: Service road
road_classes.about: Frontage or approach road, light traffic.

assumptions: The rainfall reference (60 mm a fortnight), the traffic exponent (0.5) and the score's floor and ceiling (0.05 and 10 mm/day effective) are chosen constants, not fitted ones. They are the first thing to re-fit against a season of real readings.
Bundled rainfall figures are approximate monthly normals, not a forecast. Post a real forecast to /api/rainfall and it is used instead.
Traffic counts default to a class table until a municipality supplies its own.
